core_obligations: Translate the affine case: Spec(A) over k is geometrically irreducible exactly when A is, which is immediate from the definitions (proof lines 1429-1431).

Record the topological facts used repeatedly: irreducibility passes to nonempty opens, nonempty opens of an irreducible space meet, and a scheme with irreducible affine opens is irreducible; from these the final sentence and the implications (1) to (2) to (3) to (4) follow (proof lines 1432-1439).

Close the cycle: if a nonempty cover by pairwise intersecting geometrically irreducible opens exists, then after any field extension the base change again has such a cover, hence is irreducible, so (4) implies (1) (proof lines 1439-1442).
proof_roadmap: Topological facts and the easy implications (proof lines 1432-1439).
Stability of the last condition under base change (proof lines 1439-1442).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives four equivalent conditions for a scheme X over a field k: geometric irreducibility of X, geometric irreducibility of the coordinate ring of every nonempty affine open, irreducibility of X plus geometric irreducibility of the coordinate rings of the members of one affine open covering, and the existence of a nonempty open covering by geometrically irreducible pieces which pairwise intersect; it also records that every nonempty open subscheme of a geometrically irreducible scheme is geometrically irreducible (statement lines 1404-1426). The proof reduces the affine case to the algebra definition, then uses the topological facts that irreducibility passes to nonempty opens, that two nonempty opens of an irreducible space meet, and that a scheme whose affine opens are all irreducible is irreducible; the easy implications follow, and the last condition implies irreducibility after every base change because a cover by pairwise intersecting irreducible opens stays of that form (proof lines 1428-1442). The claim is H2: a short cycle of implications whose content is the observation that the last condition is stable under base change, making it a Zariski-local criterion.
